overview.title: Brief History Of EIA In India
overview.definition: Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) is a statutory process used to evaluate the environmental consequences of a proposed project or development prior to decision-making, ensuring sustainable integration of ecological concerns into economic planning.
overview.importanceInUpsc: EIA is a perennial favorite in UPSC Prelims (Environment/Governance) and Mains (GS Paper III: Environment Conservation/Development vs. Environment debate).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Brief History Of EIA In India.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.

sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Genesis**: EIA in India began in 1976-77 for river valley projects under the Planning Commission.
• **Statutory Backing**: Derived from Section 3 of the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**, which empowers the Central Government to restrict areas for industrial operations.
• **Evolutionary Milestone**: The first EIA Notification was issued in **1994** under the EPA, 1986, making environmental clearance mandatory for specific projects.
• **Key Metric**: The **2006 Notification** decentralized the process by creating State Level Environment Impact Assessment Authorities (SEIAA).

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Categorization into A (Central) and B (State); introduced Screening, Scoping, Public Consultation, Appraisal.
Most critical for Prelims; core procedural steps.

items.definition: A body of experts that evaluates projects and recommends clearance to the Ministry; essential for technical scrutiny.
A mandatory process under the 2006 notification allowing local stakeholders to voice concerns; often a point of legal contention.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **PARIVESH Portal**: Pro-Active and Responsive facilitation by Interactive, Virtuous and Environmental Single-window Hub for automated clearance tracking.
• **EIA Draft 2020**: Proposed changes regarding post-facto clearance and reduction in public consultation time.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Post-facto clearance legality, dilution of public participation, and lack of post-clearance monitoring.
• **Solutions**: Strengthening the National Board for Wildlife (NBWL) and integrating Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA).

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'S-S-P-A' (The 4 stages of 2006 EIA).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Screening (Is it needed?), Scoping (What to study?), Public Consultation (People's voice), Appraisal (Final review).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the '1994 Notification' with the '1986 Act'. Remember: The Act is the parent legislation; the Notification is the subordinate legislation.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Developmental vs. Environmental Trade-off' and mention the 'Precautionary Principle' as the bedrock of EIA.

keyTakeaways: EIA in India is a statutory requirement under the EPA, 1986.
The 2006 Notification shifted the focus from centralized to decentralized appraisal (Category A vs B).
Public consultation is a mandatory procedural step, though subject to specific exemptions.
